==Personality==
Edward Newgate was a cheerful and carefree person during his younger years, prior to commanding his own ship and becoming known as Whitebeard. Due to being an orphan who grew up in poverty, Newgate had a strong desire for a family, which he saw as the greatest treasure one could have. Despite his peers considering this to be strange and humorous, Newgate was never ashamed of this wish.{{Qref|name=Past}}

His reign on the sea, reputation, and foreboding power made him seemingly overconfident and fearless.{{Qref|chap=434|page=15|ep=316|Whitebeard claims that he has nothing to fear.}} In initial appearances, he seemed unable to see any cause for alarm on any decision he made and refused all advice given to him, such as his nurse telling him not to drink heavily{{Qref|chap=234|page=11|ep=151|Whitebeard refuses to stop drinking despite his nurse's advice.}} or [[Shanks]] warning him of [[Marshall D. Teach|Blackbeard]].{{Qref|name=c434|chap=434|page=14|ep=316|Whitebeard refuses to heed Shanks's request for him to stop Ace's hunt for Blackbeard.}} However, he was much more thoughtful than he initially appeared to be. Actions that initially seemed to be the result of thoughtless or headstrong bravado actually had strong reasons backing them. For instance, his loud declaration that [[Fish-Man Island]] belonged to him freed the island from all invading [[pirate]]s and [[slavery]],{{Qref|name=Fish-Man Island|chap=645|page=6-7|ep=567|Whitebeard declares Fish-Man Island to be his territory.}} and his insistence that Blackbeard be punished was merely a cover for Ace, who had set out after him against Whitebeard's wishes.{{Qref|name=Claim|chap=552|page=15-16|ep=461|ep2=462|Whitebeard covers for Ace defying his orders by taking responsibility for his hunt for Blackbeard.}}

{{Cquote|''I am only one man with one heart...Call me a demon, call me a monster...but I can't be the strongest forever...!!!''|2=Whitebeard's response to his status as the "Strongest Man in the World".{{Qref|name=Mortality|chap=563|ep=472|page=16|Whitebeard thinks about his mortality.}}}}

Though he may seem to have an overgrown ego, Whitebeard knew deep down that he was nothing but a single man and was fully aware of his own mortality.{{Qref|name=Mortality}} He knew that the youths of the next generation were the keys to the future and that their lives were far more important than his own. Because of this, he was not afraid to sacrifice himself for the safety of those he considered his children.{{Qref|chap=569|page=11-12|ep=478|Whitebeard states that he must watch over the futures of his sons.}} Like [[Gol D. Roger]], Whitebeard believed that a child should not be responsible for their parents' sins.{{Qref|name=Assurance|chap=563|page=13|ep=472|Whitebeard tells Squard that Ace does not bear Roger's sins and is no different from any other of his sons.}} Yet another belief he held is that any path a man wished to follow in life was fine by him, as long as they did not regret it.{{Qref|name="New Age"}}

Despite his fierce reputation, Whitebeard was a compassionate man, having adopted countless people of different backgrounds into his crew as his foster children, such as [[Squard]], whose life was devastated by Roger killing his crew, or Teach, who requested to join his crew due to being homeless. [[Polo Marco|Marco]] stated that the main reason the Whitebeard Pirates held such strong loyalty to their captain was due to Newgate's paternal-like attitude, deeply caring for them like a father. Contrary to the tyrannical [[Kaidou]] and the insane [[Charlotte Linlin|Big Mom]], Whitebeard used his power and influence as one of the [[Four Emperors]] for humanitarian purposes. He liberated and protected Fish-Man Island from slavery, an act that touched the hearts of the normally human-distrusting citizens of [[Ryugu Kingdom]], and invested the majority of his riches to support his homeland of [[Sphinx (Location)|Sphinx]], a once poor, lawless island.{{Qref|name=c909|chap=909|page=5-7|ep=890|Marco explains to Nekomamushi the plight of Sphinx and how Whitebeard covertly sent humanitarian aid to support the citizens.}} Whitebeard was understanding and forgiving of his subordinates, going to great lengths to rescue any who were in great danger, no matter the cost.{{Qref|name=Arrival|chap=551|page=18-19|ep=461|Whitebeard arrives at Marineford to save Ace.}} He was naturally protective of his family and did not tolerate the idea of letting a crewmate join someone else's crew, especially a rival one. In fact, the notion of separating himself from just one of them, even for a short time, infuriated him. Even if he did accept doing so, it was reluctantly and while showing much annoyance.{{Qref|chap=966|page=11-13|ep=966}}

Whitebeard was very careful about choosing a person to be included in his crew, depending on their personality and nature. This cautiousness mainly stemmed from his time as a member of the [[Rocks Pirates]], as the violent and poor relationship among the members of that crew left a negative impact on Whitebeard.{{Qref|chap=964|page=2|ep=963|Whitebeard initially turned down Oden's request to join his crew because of his wild nature and states how such character traits were an issue on the Rocks Pirates.}}{{Qref|name=c1096}} For this reason, Whitebeard was fully against letting someone like [[Kouzuki Oden]] join his crew, since the [[Samurai]] was rebellious by nature. Still, Whitebeard showed enough open-mindedness to give Oden a chance to prove himself in a challenge and eventually allowed the [[Kuri]] daimyo to be part of his crew after the latter prioritized the life of an [[Kouzuki Toki|innocent woman]] over the challenge itself. Also, while he held reservations regarding [[Marshall D. Teach]], he nevertheless allowed the boy to join his crew for being an orphan with nowhere else to go; this turned out to be a mistake that Whitebeard would come to regret.

A distinguishing feature of Whitebeard's nature was his high moral standards: he never forgave the death of a crewmate by another and believed that a man could not live without some form of honor code.{{Qref|name=c434}} When confronted by Blackbeard, he intended to avenge [[Thatch]], despite being close to death at the time.{{Qref|chap=576|page=6|ep=485|Whitebeard declares that he will kill Blackbeard in order to avenge Thatch.}} However, he was willing to go against his personal code under certain circumstances if he felt the risk would not be worth the safety of his crew.{{Qref|name=Don't Hunt|chap=552|page=14|ep=461|Whitebeard tells Ace to let Blackbeard go because he feels uneasy about him.}}{{Qref|chap=999|page=12-13|Whitebeard tells Ace they will not confront Kaidou at Onigashima due to potential casualties.|ep=1014}}

Whitebeard seemed to enjoy talking about the past; when Shanks visited his [[Moby Dick|ship]], the first thing Newgate did was recollect his memories from the last twenty-two years, particularly those involving old rivals like Roger, [[Monkey D. Garp|Garp]], and [[Sengoku]].{{Qref|name=Nostalgia|chap=434|page=9-11|ep=316|Whitebeard talks about the past with Shanks.}}{{Qref|chap=559|page=5|ep=468|Whitebeard notes that seeing Buggy takes him back.}} People that were children at that time were still viewed as children in Whitebeard's eyes, no matter how powerful they had grown since.{{Qref|name=c434}}{{Qref|name=Aokiji Tyke|chap=553|page=5|ep=462|Whitebeard calls Aokiji a tyke.}} Despite fond memories of his time as a pirate captain, Whitebeard was not proud of his former association with the Rocks Pirates due to the lack of camaraderie among members; thus, he rarely referred to those times except in a negative tone.

Regardless of his poor health at the time, Whitebeard liked drinking, to the point that bringing and sharing a drink with him—preferably of high quality and very expensive—was viewed as an adequately respectful gesture to engage him in conversation. This was seen in his encounters with Shanks,{{Qref|chap=434|page=8|ep=316|Shanks brings Whitebeard some sake from West Blue.}} Gol D. Roger,{{Qref|name=Whitebeard and Roger|chap=576|page=12|ep=485|Whitebeard drinks with Roger prior to the latter's death.}} and [[Shiki]]; still, this did not guarantee complete cooperation from him, judging from the nature of these conversations.{{Qref|name=zero}}{{Qref|chap=434|page=14-17|ep=316|The conversation between Whitebeard and Shanks regarding Ace and Blackbeard turns violent.}}

Like other characters in One Piece, Whitebeard had a [[Laughter Style|unique laugh]], which was "Gu ra ra ra ra." {{Qref|chap=434|page=7|ep=316|Whitebeard laughs.}} Like [[Perona]], his laugh was similar to the name of his Devil Fruit, the [[Gura Gura no Mi]]. However, in the anime (before the Marineford Arc) and [[Gigant Battle]], his laugh was changed to a regular "Ha ha ha ha ha." The American Shonen Jump, and the English dub, still retain this version of the laugh, even after the switch in the Japanese version.

==Relationships==
===Crew===
{{Cquote|Whitebeard sold out his people?! That's ridiculous!! His loyalty to his men is legendary!!|Capone Bege on Whitebeard.{{Qref|chap=565|page=3|ep=574}}}}

[[File:Whitebeard Pirate Division Commanders.png|thumb|210px|Whitebeard along with his Division Commanders.]]

Whitebeard considered every single member of his crew, as well as his subordinate crews, his "sons." His strong love for his crew and subordinate crews traced all the way back to before he even had a crew, when he stated that the one thing he wanted more than anything was a family.{{Qref|name=Past}}

Any crewmember from Whitebeard's crew who killed another crewmember was to be hunted down by the commander of that former crew member's division.{{Qref|chap=552|page=14|ep=461|Ace states that he needs to hunt down Blackbeard because Thatch was a member of his division.}} Whitebeard's strong stand against crewmate killing was based on his fatherly stance over every member of his crew; as a result of this treatment, the whole crew affectionately referred to him as {{Nihongo|"Pops" or "Old Man"|オヤジ|Oyaji|an informal variation of "father"}}.{{Qref|chap=552|page=12|ep=461|Marco explains why all of Whitebeard's crew members refer to him as their father.}} However, Whitebeard did not force commanders to hunt down wayward crew members if he had an uneasy feeling about the situation; in the case of Blackbeard, Whitebeard tried to make an exception and stop Ace from hunting him down, but Ace did so anyway for the sake of Whitebeard's honor.{{Qref|name=Don't Hunt}}

This was not blind loyalty, as Whitebeard was willing to go to war with the [[World Government]] to save Ace.{{Qref|name=Arrival}} In addition, Whitebeard took full responsibility for the actions of his crew and kept a stern outward appearance for non-crew members, falsely claiming to outsiders that he ordered Ace to hunt down Blackbeard.{{Qref|name=Claim}} Whitebeard also treated all of his "sons" and "daughters" equally and claimed to Squard that Ace was no different than any other, despite being Roger's son.{{Qref|name=Assurance}} In battle, while this unshakable bond between him and his crew stood, Whitebeard's subordinates knew better than to get in the way of their captain.{{Qref|chap=564|page=7|ep=473|Whitebeard's subordinates tell each other to not get in his way.}}

====Marco====
Out of everybody within his crew, [[Polo Marco|Marco]] was perhaps the closest person Whitebeard had to a right-hand man. During the initial stages of the Marineford War, Marco stood right by Whitebeard's side, informing him of battlefield intel, protecting him from long-range assaults, listening to his comments and orders; he was also the only one to rush to Whitebeard's aid after the latter got stabbed by Squard, showing little tolerance to the perpetrator for harming his captain.{{Qref|chap=563|page=4|ep=472|Marco restrains Squard after the latter stabs Whitebeard.}} Later, Marco attempted to assist his captain in fighting Blackbeard, but was ultimately ordered to stand down.{{Qref|chap=576|page=6-7|ep=485|Whitebeard orders Marco to not interfere.}} After Whitebeard's death, Marco was moved to tears, much like the rest of his crewmates, and made sure to carry out his captain's final order to escort Luffy to safety. Marco was also the one who instigated the [[Payback War]] against [[Marshall D. Teach|Blackbeard]], gathering the remnants of the Whitebeard Pirates to hunt down the crew's traitor and man responsible for Whitebeard and Ace's deaths, but failed to accomplish his revenge.{{Qref|chap=820|ep=773|page=11-12|The Ninja-Pirate-Mink-Samurai Alliance speak of the Payback War.}}

As a testament to Whitebeard and Marco's closeness, the latter was aware of the former's childhood circumstances as an orphan of [[Sphinx (Location)|Sphinx]], which led to Whitebeard's career of piracy. Since his old captain had spent much of his fortune aiding his struggling homeland, Marco found himself with the duty of protecting the one thing that still remained from Whitebeard's past, becoming a local [[doctor]] who took care of the health of the locals. Marco teared up when he told [[Nekomamushi]] about Whitebeard's love for the land he had been born into, knowing that it was the reason his captain was so stingy with money.{{Qref|name=c909}}

====Portgas D. Ace====
{{Cquote|It'd be a shame if you died here, kid. If you still want to wreak havoc on this sea, bear my name on your back and go wild as much as you like! Become my son!|Whitebeard tells [[Portgas D. Ace|Ace]] to join his crew.{{Qref|chap=552|ep=461|page=10|Whitebeard offers Ace a chance to join his crew.}}}}

[[File:Ace Bows to Whitebeard.png|thumb|left|250px|Ace bows to Whitebeard in their final moments together.]]
Whitebeard first became aware of [[Portgas D. Ace]] while the latter was still a rookie, being curious and impressed by the rapid growth and progress of the youngster's career as a pirate captain. 

After easily defeating him, Whitebeard eventually revealed himself to be a magnanimous man to Ace and his crew, giving him the chance to join his family as his son.{{Qref|chap=552|page=9-13|ep=461|Whitebeard defeats and recruits Ace.}} Initially, Ace refused this offer and attempted to kill Whitebeard nearly a hundred times, only to fail at each one. As he further bonded with Whitebeard's crewmates, who already treated him as family, Ace eventually grew to respect Whitebeard so much that he viewed him as a proper father figure due to his hatred of his actual father, Gol D. Roger. Ace claimed to Sengoku that he believed Whitebeard would become Pirate King.

As Ace's respect for Whitebeard grew, so did his honor as one of the Whitebeard Pirates. Because of this, he was one of the most outraged members regarding [[Thatch]]'s murder, viewing such a thing as an unforgivable offense to Whitebeard's ideals. Although Whitebeard advised him not to venture into the hunt for [[Marshall D. Teach|Teach]], Ace left without permission, and, in the end, Whitebeard took responsibility for Ace's mistakes without hesitation by going to Marineford to save him from execution.{{Qref|chap=552|page=14|ep=462|Whitebeard speaks with Ace just prior to the Summit War of Marineford.}} After Ace was freed from the execution platform, Whitebeard asked him if he had been a good father to him and felt satisfied once Ace stated that he was a good father.{{Qref|chap=573|page=8|ep=482|Ace thanks Whitebeard for everything.}} Ace's death was enough to make Whitebeard stop holding back the full destructiveness of his Devil Fruit, with him targeting Ace's killer, Akainu, almost immediately after.

====Kouzuki Oden====
From their first meeting and their brief fight, Whitebeard understood how dangerous and strong [[Kouzuki Oden|Oden]] was.{{Qref|name=c963p15|chap=963|page=15|ep=963|Newgate senses Oden approaching him.}} He initially disagreed on taking Oden into the crew, as he saw him as a chaotic type and not capable of submitting to anyone, but eventually, after Oden passed a hard test of endurance, even after the [[samurai]] threw out the challenge just to save a [[Kouzuki Toki|nearby woman]] in need, Whitebeard decided to take him on board his ship as his brother and promised him the adventure of a lifetime.{{Qref|chap=964|page=15|ep=964}}

During the time Oden was onboard his ship, Whitebeard became close to Oden, even regarding him as a brotherly figure. He got very angry when Roger asked him to borrow Oden and then got annoyed when Oden himself asked him to allow it, hating just the idea that he could leave his crew, even if only for a short time. He let Oden go without saying goodbye but still ordered his crew to leave some supplies for him and his family.{{Qref|name=c966p12|chap=966|page=12|ep=966}}

Whitebeard was well aware of Oden's incredible strength and entrusted him with the command of the second division. He left the command vacant for a long time also after his departure, since he had not received any news of his death until several years after it happened. Whitebeard considered Ace arrogant for thinking he could defeat Kaidou when even Oden couldn't defeat him.{{Qref|chap=999|page=14|Whitebeard talks about avenging Oden's death.|ep=1014|name=c999}}

====Izou====
Initially, [[Izou]] had a hostile relationship with Whitebeard, which stemmed from the painful and humiliating treatment Izou's master, Oden, was receiving as part of the challenge Whitebeard had given the daimyo in order to join his crew. Izou stated that he would make Whitebeard pay for putting his master through so much trouble.{{Qref|chap=964|page=7|ep=963|Izou threatens Whitebeard.}} This hostility dissipated a bit when Oden was formally inducted into the Whitebeard Pirates, with Izou sticking around for Oden's sake.{{Qref|chap=964|page=14|ep=964|Whitebeard replies to Izou's threats.}}

Izou eventually grew fond of his new group and became a full-fledged member, preferring to stay with the Whitebeard Pirates when Oden decided to join the Roger Pirates. He was eventually promoted to commander of the sixteenth division of the crew, showing that he had earned Whitebeard's respect as a leader and fighter.{{Qref|name=c966p12}}

===Subordinate Crews===
Aside from their own 1,600-member crew,{{Qref|name=Structure|data=yellow|The Whitebeard Pirates' size and organization are outlined.}} the Whitebeard Pirates had many subordinate crews working in the New World. Each one of the pirate captains was an infamous pirate who had made a name for him or herself in the New World. There seemed to be at least 43 crews underneath Whitebeard.{{Qref|chap=551|page=12-13|ep=460|The Marines comment on the incoming ships and their captains.}} Whitebeard treated all of his long-time subordinate crews just like his own crew, as though they were his own sons, though some of them were originally from the main crew before becoming captains of their own crews.{{Qref|chap=963|page=14-15|ep=962}} They all seemed to know Ace, at least, and were willing to help Whitebeard's cause when Ace was about to be executed at Marineford; however, they were not aware that Ace was Roger's son until around the time Ace died. These New World subordinate crews included "Bohemian Knight" [[Doma]], "Thunder Lord" [[McGuy]], the [[Decalvan Brothers]], "Great Whirlpool Spider" [[Squard]],{{Qref|chap=551|page=12|ep=460|The Marines identify some of the captains among Whitebeard's subordinate crews.}} [[Little Oars Jr.]],{{Qref|chap=554|page=14-15|ep=463|Little Oars Jr. enters the battle.}} and the "Ice Witch" [[Whitey Bay]].{{Qref|chap=556|page=12|ep=462|Whitey Bay arrives at the Paramount War.}}

====Squard====
[[File:Whitebeard Forgives Squard.png|thumb|210px|Whitebeard hugs and forgives his 'son'.]]

After losing his entire crew to Roger, Squard was taken in by Whitebeard, who treated him like a son and saved him from the loneliness of losing all of his comrades. Squard, in return, thought of Whitebeard as a father figure but felt betrayed when he thought that Whitebeard was planning to sacrifice all of his subordinate crews to save Ace, leading him to stab the Emperor in a surprise attack. When Whitebeard proved otherwise, Squard broke down in tears at his mistake.{{Qref|chap=563|page=5-7, 11-13|ep=472|Squard accuses Whitebeard of sacrificing his subordinate crews, but is proved wrong.}} He later attempted to redeem himself at the cost of his own life by charging head-first into battle, but Whitebeard himself stopped and reprimanded him.{{Qref|chap=572|page=11-14|ep=481|Whitebeard prevents Squard from leading a suicidal charge.}}{{-}}

===Friends and Allies===
====Jinbe====
Because of his role as a protector of Fish-Man Island, Whitebeard was considered a hero by many [[Fish-Men]],{{Qref|name=Fish-Man Island}} in particular [[Jinbe]] of the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]]. Jinbe had expressed many times that he owed a great deal of gratitude to the Emperor{{Qref|chap=529|page=2-4|ep=430|Jinbe explains why he feels indebted to Whitebeard.}} and refused to participate in the war against Whitebeard, even if it meant losing his Warlord of the Sea title and being imprisoned in [[Impel Down]].{{Qref|chap=523|page=10|ep=417|Jinbe is revealed to be in Impel Down after refusing to join the war against Whitebeard.}} When Jinbe arrived at Marineford with the other escapees from Impel Down, the first thing he did was announce his formal resignation from the Warlords to Sengoku.

Over the years, Jinbe's respect for Whitebeard had grown to the point where he was ready to declare himself an adversary to anyone or anything with ill intent upon the Emperor's life, which is why he immediately engaged in battle against Ace on their first encounter, since Ace was out to assassinate Whitebeard at that time.{{Qref|chap=552|page=7|ep=461|Jinbe confronts Ace during his attempt to assassinate Whitebeard.}}

====Monkey D. Luffy====
[[File:Luffy and Whitebeard During Battle Of Marineford.png|thumb|left|210px|Whitebeard and Luffy preparing to save Ace.]]

Whitebeard seemed to have some form of respect for [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]] after hearing about him from both Ace and Shanks; Ace had shown excitement that Luffy was on the Grand Line,{{Qref|name=c557|chap=557|page=15|ep=466|Whitebeard remembers a young Shanks and Ace showing him Luffy's first bounty poster.}} and Shanks had stated that he had given up his arm on a "bet on the [[Pirate#The New Age|New Age]]," referring to Luffy.{{Qref|name="New Age"|chap=434|page=11|ep=316|Shanks claims he bet his arm on "the New Age."}} After showing his fierce tenacity, Luffy had managed to gain Whitebeard's respect.{{Qref|chap=557|page=16|ep=466|Whitebeard grins after Luffy declares that he will be Pirate King.}} Whitebeard went as far as assigning his top commander, [[Polo Marco|Marco]], to act as Luffy's bodyguard during the war and "would not have forgiven him" if Luffy had died.{{Qref|chap=558|page=17|ep=467|Whitebeard orders Marco to protect Luffy.}}

As the war went on, his respect for Luffy increased after witnessing Luffy's [[Haki/Supreme King Haki|true potential]], and Whitebeard decided to command all his forces to fully support Luffy with all their might, a decision that even surprised his own men. This also marks the first time that Whitebeard called him by his name, Straw Hat Luffy, instead of "brat," proving that Whitebeard came to acknowledge him and his strength through the course of the war.{{Qref|chap=570|page=4-5|ep=479|Whitebeard commands his forces to support Luffy.}} Luffy respected Whitebeard as well, believing that anyone whom Ace admires cannot be a bad person, and was willing to intercept an attack from Crocodile aimed at Whitebeard's life before he even met him in person.{{Qref|chap=557|page=14-15|ep=466|Luffy protects Whitebeard from Crocodile's attack and explains his reason for doing so.}}

Before the end of his life, in his final words to [[Marshall D. Teach|Blackbeard]] and [[Sengoku]], it is implied that he believes Luffy is the person [[Gol D. Roger]] has been waiting for and that he will be the one to find [[One Piece]].

====Neptune====
Whitebeard was an old friend of [[Neptune|King Neptune]]. Their friendship stemmed from when they first drank together, and Whitebeard protected Fish-Man Island from slavery due to this friendship. Though it is unknown how they became friends, it is known that they had been friends for quite some time, as Neptune helped Whitebeard out a lot during his younger days.{{Qref|name=Fish-Man Island}}

===Protectorates===
Before his demise, Whitebeard had a number of locations under his protection.{{Qref|chap=529|page=4|ep=430|Jinbe notes that Whitebeard holds many territories under his protection.}} Most of them seemed to be on the brink of pirate raids, and it was only by being "owned" under his name that they were kept stable and safe, thereby earning the Emperor the gratitude of the citizens; consequentially, these territories immediately became vulnerable after his death.{{Qref|name=Foodvalten|chap=581|page=7-8|ep=490|Brownbeard conquers Foodvalten after Whitebeard's death.}} At least one other Emperor, [[Charlotte Linlin|Big Mom]], placed Fish-Man Island under her protection{{Qref|chap=610|page=13|ep=529|Pappug reveals that Big Mom is currently protecting Fish-Man Island.}} while [[Foodvalten]] fell to [[Chadros Higelyges|Brownbeard]].{{Qref|name=Foodvalten}} The status of Whitebeard's other former territories is currently unknown, but Blackbeard appears to have taken over most of them during his ascent to Four Emperors status, as he has over two decades of experience with the Whitebeard Pirates and thus knows which islands they were protecting.{{Qref|name=Islands + Four Emperors|chap=650|page=7-8|ep=570|Jinbe reveals Blackbeard's recent activities to the Straw Hats.}}

Among Whitebeard's known territories, his own homeland of [[Sphinx (Location)|Sphinx]] was the most important to him. Due to the high costs of the [[World Noble]]s' heavenly tribute being impossible for a poverty-stricken place like Sphinx to afford, the island suffered from constant pirate and slaver attacks without government protection. A young, orphaned Newgate had to grow under those oppressive conditions, leading to his life as a pirate, although he never valued treasure as much as the idea of family. As such, Whitebeard dedicated a majority of his riches for humanitarian aid towards Sphinx, having built a peaceful village for the locals to live in.

===Enemies===
{{Cquote|Roger... Garp... Sengoku... there aren't very many people who know about the sea back then.|Whitebeard about his respected enemies.{{Qref|name=Old-Timers|chap=434|ep=316|page=9|Whitebeard notes that very few people remain who remember the sea from Roger's era.}}}}

====Gol D. Roger====
[[File:Roger and Whitebeard laughing.png|thumb|210px|Roger and Whitebeard laughing with each other.]]

Despite having been rivals with [[Gol D. Roger]], Whitebeard held great respect for him. They seemingly had multiple duels throughout their lives, with one instance in particular leading to a friendly gift exchange between their crewmembers after three days of endless battling. During this occasion, Whitebeard and Roger held a casual conversation with Kouzuki Oden joining in, showing both captains were comfortable with each other's presence. However, Whitebeard did not like Roger's attempt to "borrow" Oden as a crewmate for the Roger Pirates and was further angered when Oden did show interest in switching crews.

Not long before his death, Roger met with Whitebeard on an island to have what seemed to be an entirely cordial drinking session, with Roger even offering to give the location of Laugh Tale to Whitebeard, and when Whitebeard asked Roger about the [[Will of D.]], Roger willingly told him about it.{{Qref|name=Whitebeard and Roger}} Upon learning that Ace was his rival's son, Whitebeard did not see his bloodline as an inconvenience and even tried to inspire Ace to respect Roger as his father.{{Qref|chap=552|page=13|ep=461|Whitebeard learns of Ace's lineage.}}

====Impel Down Convicts====
Whitebeard made many enemies over the years besides the other Emperors and the World Government. Many prisoners in the lower levels of [[Impel Down]] wished to kill him because of personal grudges.{{Qref|chap=529|page=6-7|ep=430|The prisoners in level 6 of Impel Down express their desire to kill Whitebeard.}}

====Crocodile====
[[File:Crocodile Tries to Kill Whitebeard.png|thumb|left|210px|Crocodile attempting to take Whitebeard's life at Marineford.]]

At some point in the past, right after attaining the position of one of the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]], [[Crocodile]] suffered a humiliating defeat against Whitebeard in the [[New World]], enough to shatter his ambitions of becoming Pirate King for a while. Knowing he could not obtain the title of Pirate King without military might to challenge the likes of Whitebeard, Crocodile fled back to [[Paradise]], where he settled in [[Arabasta Kingdom|Arabasta]] in order to found [[Baroque Works]] and eventually conquer the kingdom so he could search it for one of the [[Ancient Weapons]], [[Pluton]].{{Qref|name=s78|sbs=78|page=86|Whitebeard and Crocodile's history is revealed.}}

Crocodile was one of the many Impel Down convicts who sought revenge against Whitebeard. While he did attempt to take Whitebeard's life at Marineford, he was stopped from doing so by Luffy. From then on, Crocodile took a neutral role in the war, fighting both Marines and Whitebeard's men, with Whitebeard himself showing some annoyance towards Crocodile's attacks on his crew.

Despite his genuine grudge against the Emperor, Crocodile seemed to have at least some degree of respect for him. This was evident when he became extremely disappointed and angry at Whitebeard's failing health, stating that he no longer looked like the same man who defeated him years ago. Still, by the end of the war, Crocodile started fighting for Whitebeard's side, as he preferred the Marines to not have a complete win.

====Marines====
Whitebeard respected both [[Monkey D. Garp]] and [[Sengoku]], a respect that was mutual. He considered them among the few people that knew the seas from Roger's era who are still alive in the present.{{Qref|name=Old-Timers}} On the other hand, he considered other younger Marines to be "brats" and refused to give any of them, including the powerful [[admiral]]s, much respect.{{Qref|name=Aokiji Tyke}}{{Qref|chap=554|page=11|ep=463|Whitebeard calls Akainu a brat.}} However, [[Sakazuki]] earned Whitebeard's wrath for killing Ace, and Whitebeard brutally injured him.{{Qref|name=Akainu Beatdown|chap=575|page=6-7|ep=480|Whitebeard brutally injures Akainu for killing Ace.}}

====Marshall D. Teach====
[[File:Whitebeard vs Blackbeard Pirates.png|thumb|210px|Teach and the Blackbeard Pirates attack Whitebeard.]]

[[Marshall D. Teach]], also known as Blackbeard, was one of Whitebeard's oldest crewmates, having joined the crew at twelve years old. When Teach claimed to be an orphan with nowhere else to go, Whitebeard quickly allowed him to join out of sympathy. Though it is unknown if Whitebeard knew that Teach was the son of his former captain [[Rocks D. Xebec]].

Teach ultimately became Whitebeard's greatest enemy for killing [[Thatch]] and enabling Ace's capture and execution. Claiming that Blackbeard alone was the only one whom he refused to consider his son, Whitebeard attempted to take Blackbeard's life prior to his death, calling him an arrogant fool that was never worthy of being a part of his crew.{{Qref|chap=576|page=6-9|ep=485|Whitebeard declares that Blackbeard is not his son and attempts to kill him.}} Just before dying, Whitebeard openly declared that Blackbeard was not worthy of being Roger's successor.{{Qref|chap=576|page=13|ep=485|Whitebeard declares Blackbeard to be unworthy of succeeding Roger.}} His last thought being his regret for allowing Teach to hurt his foster family. After Whitebeard's death, Blackbeard stole his Devil Fruit powers, conquered his territories, and usurped his post as one of the Four Emperors.{{Qref|name=Islands + Four Emperors}} Whitebeard appears to be one of the very few people Teach genuinely fears, as shown when he pathetically begged him for mercy while being stomped on the ground before landing the final blow on his former captain. {{Qref|chap=576|page=7|ep=485|Teach begs Whitebeard for mercy before landing the final blow.}}
{{-}}

===Four Emperors===
====Shanks====
[[File:Shanks Reunited With Whitebeard.png|thumb|left|210px|Shanks meets with Whitebeard, offering him sake to talk.]]

During his many battles with the Roger Pirates, Whitebeard would notice and grow more and more familiar with [[Shanks]],{{Qref|name=c557}} since he would always spot the youngster alongside Buggy during their battles.{{Qref|name=Nostalgia}} As the years went by and the two became members of the Four Emperors, they would be considered enemies by each other's respective crews. In his first appearance, Whitebeard received a letter from Shanks delivered by the former's newest crewmate, [[Rockstar]]. However, before even reading the letter, Whitebeard threw it away, claiming that Shanks should come in person with some expensive sake if he wanted to talk.{{Qref|name=Refusal|chap=234|page=10-13|ep=151|Whitebeard refuses to read Shanks's letter and tells him to come in person.}} Most of all, he refused to accept Shanks as anything more than the kid he was 22 years ago and believed he was 100 years too young to tell him what to do.{{Qref|name=c434}}

Despite being enemies, Shanks held great respect for Whitebeard, which made him willing to lend his aid to Whitebeard by preventing the Emperor [[Kaidou]] from reaching Whitebeard, allowing him to reach Marineford without any hindrance.{{Qref|name=Four Emperors Clash|chap=533|page=3|ep=434|Shanks is revealed to have intercepted Kaidou when the latter attempted to attack Whitebeard.}} After Whitebeard's death, Shanks saved Whitebeard's crew and their other subordinate crews,{{Qref|chap=580|page=14-15|ep=489|Shanks convinces Sengoku to end the Paramount War.}} and gives Whitebeard and Ace a proper burial.{{Qref|name=Funeral|chap=590|page=8|ep=505|Shanks holds a funeral for Whitebeard and Ace.}}

====Kaidou====
In the past, they used to be part of the [[Rocks Pirates]], and Whitebeard was initially on amiable terms with the young [[Kaidou]], with the latter expressing envy for Newgate's Gura Gura no Mi and Whitebeard advising him to choose a Devil Fruit carefully, as it could affect him for life. After the [[God Valley Incident|incident]] at [[God Valley]] in which they helped Rocks against Imu, they went their separate ways to form their own crews and became Emperors. Despite their past camaraderie, Kaidou does not think highly of Whitebeard, stating that he was too soft-hearted despite being powerful. Still, he acknowledges that the once strongest man in the world had died in glory.{{Qref|chap=994|page=4|Kaidou states Roger and Whitebeard died the "right" way.|ep=1006}} Kaidou also recognized Whitebeard among the few powerful individuals capable of fighting him.{{Qref|name=c1001|chap=1001|ep=1016|page=3}}

Despite knowing and expressing contempt that Kaido had killed Oden, whom Whitebeard considered a brother, he also acknowledged Kaidou's immense power, and for this, he chose not to march into Wano Country to wage war against his crew just to avenge Oden's death, knowing that it would cause many casualties. In addition, Whitebeard warned his subordinate [[Portgas D. Ace|Ace]] that, despite Ace's own reputation and strength, he had no chance of victory against Kaidou, showing wariness of Kaidou's increase in strength over the years. {{Qref|name=c999}}

Under normal circumstances, they did not provoke each other. However, Kaidou saw an opportunity to eliminate his adversary prior to the impending [[Summit War of Marineford]] and did not hesitate to attempt to do so.{{Qref|name=Four Emperors Clash}} Two years later, Kaidou cursed Whitebeard for being able to die while he remained alive.{{Qref|chap=795|page=17|ep=739|Kaidou curses Whitebeard for having died while he could not.}}

===Rocks Pirates===
Whitebeard had been acquainted with [[Rocks D. Xebec|Rocks]] 48 years ago and eventually became a brief yet founding member of the [[Rocks Pirates]] for six years, specifically until the [[God Valley Incident]], when the crew met its downfall. At that point, he was already in possession of the Gura Gura ability, making Newgate one of their prominent members alongside Rocks himself.

Whitebeard did not seem to hold his old crew or captain in high regard, rarely talking about his time as a member, though it was clear that he was one of their more better-natured constituents and was about as welcoming as Linlin was to the young Kaidou. He even mentored the latter on what it meant to attain a Devil Fruit power when Kaidou expressed a desire to obtain one himself. And during a flashback from when the two went to [[Elbaph]], he was openly critical of Rocks brutalizing the giant prince Loki, who was a mere child at the time.{{Qref|chap=1145|page=11-12|ep=1175}} 38 years ago, as the crew arrived on [[God Valley]], he called Rocks a fool repeatedly, worrying that his antics would distract from their "mission" to recover Shakky and any treasure or Devil Fruits.{{Qref|name=c1096}} He used the Rocks Pirates as a reason for dismissing Oden joining the Whitebeard Pirates, citing the daimyo's wild, rebellious nature as being difficult to control and equating it to the other members of Rocks.{{Qref|chap=964|page=2|ep=963|Whitebeards mentions his previous crew to Oden.}}

====Rocks D. Xebec====
[[File:Rocks vs Whitebeard.png|thumb|210px|Newgate defending himself from a controlled Rocks.]]

Whitebeard reluctantly joined Rocks after losing a [[Davy Back Fight]]. Whitebeard was open about why he followed Rocks and that he didn't much care for Rocks's ambitions. He also did not respect Rocks, going as far as referring to him as a fool. Despite this, Whitebeard followed Rocks along his journey and stayed with the Rocks Pirates as long as possible. When the Rocks Pirates invaded God Valley and Rocks headed off by himself, Whitebeard was annoyed about Rocks' apparent lack of leadership and thought that Rocks shouldn't forget the big picture. Even though he didn't have much sympathy or empathy for his captain, that didn't stop Whitebeard from having enough camaraderie towards his captain to willingly help Rocks against [[Nerona Imu|Imu]] in God Valley.{{Qref|chap=1162|page=3, 16-17|ep=}} When Rocks was turned into a [[demon]] by Imu at God Valley, Whitebeard was shocked to see his former captain so changed. However, Whitebeard remained unfazed by Rocks when he witnessed Rocks assaulting both Kaidou and Linlin before he defended himself against Rocks.{{Qref|chap=1164|page=8-9}} Whitebeard later appeared to be untouched by the previous events and Rocks's sudden betrayal, as he didn't care about finding Rocks or helping him against Roger and Garp.{{Qref|chap=1165|ep=}} Even years later, Whitebeard would never talk about his time in the Rocks Pirates or Rocks himself, signaling that he didn't care much about Rocks to remember the time he had in the Rocks Pirates or with Rocks.

====Shiki====
[[File:Shiki and Whitebeard.png|thumb|left|210px|Shiki and Whitebeard discuss Shiki's plans after his escape.]]

In the past, Whitebeard had been acquainted with [[Shiki]] no later than 48 years ago, and both would eventually be founding members of the Rocks Pirates. They appeared to have a sort of rivalry back then, as Shiki threw a bomb at him while they were raiding the [[International Philanthropy Federation]] and later grew annoyed at Whitebeard for acting like his leader.{{Qref|name=c1096|chap=1096|page=9|ep=1130}} After the God Valley Incident, they went their separate ways to form their own respective crews.

Despite this, Shiki did not appear to have a serious grudge against Whitebeard; he thought of him as a strong man and able to take over Roger's dominion of the sea, as he said when they were drinking together on the [[Moby Dick]] and speaking about old times. Whitebeard was mostly annoyed with Shiki's ramblings at the time and even threatened to have Shiki thrown into the sea but seemingly knew he had something planned, being familiar with the Golden Lion's penchant for schemes.{{Qref|name=zero}}

====Buckingham Stussy====
Miss [[Buckingham Stussy]] is the self-proclaimed lover of Whitebeard and mother of [[Edward Weevil]]. Whitebeard has known Stussy for at least 48 years, and they were fellow crewmembers of the Rocks Pirates.{{Qref|chap=909|page=7|ep=890}} She claims and/or believes herself to have been his lover, and that he is the father of her son, which she believes makes her and Weevil the rightful heirs to Whitebeard's fortune.{{Qref|chap=802|ep=752|page=9-10|Buckin claims that she was Whitebeard's lover and that his fortune belongs to her and Weevil.}} Though this claim is dubious to the point of likely being false, as Whitebeard has made it clear he was not interested in her romantically and reacted to her advances in annoyance. However, by 38 years ago, he was comfortable with Stussy placing herself atop his shoulder.{{Qref|name=c1096}} although he was more interested in saving Shakky, much to Stussy's annoyance.

===Other===
====Edward Weevil====
[[Edward Weevil]] claims to be Edward Newgate's biological son.{{Qref|chap=802|page=8|ep=752|Weevil's infobox lists him as being the self-proclaimed son of Whitebeard.}} However, many doubt this claim, and it is unconfirmed whether he actually is Whitebeard's biological son or not.{{Qref|chap=802|page=6|ep=751|A Marine notes that many doubt Weevil's claim of being Whitebeard's son.}} Weevil and his mother seek to obtain Whitebeard's fortune due to their belief that they are his rightful heirs, and to this end they have been hunting down Whitebeard's surviving [[Whitebeard Pirates|allies]] and their subordinate crews in order to claim it. Weevil also wishes to avenge Whitebeard's death by killing the Emperor [[Marshall D. Teach]], indicating that, at the very least, he truly believes himself to be Whitebeard's son.{{Qref|chap=802|page=10-11|ep=752|Weevil and Buckin discuss their respective goals of avenging Whitebeard and claiming his treasure.}}

====Loki====
Upon meeting [[Loki]] as a child 48 years ago when he was crying from being ostracized by his people, he was surprised by how big he was but also treated the young giant with sympathy and asked him why he was crying. He was also appalled by his captain injuring him in a fight.

====Shakuyaku====
Like the rest of his former crewmates, Newgate was also infatuated with [[Shakuyaku]] and would do anything for her. He even requested that she put all of the drinks he had at her [[Shakky's Rip-off Bar|bar]] on Rocks' tab. When she was kidnapped, he was shown to be visibly upset and even desired to rescue her at the [[God Valley Incident]], much to Stussy's fury.

==Abilities and Powers==
[[File:Luffy Among Legends.png|thumb|210px|Kaidou envisions Whitebeard behind Luffy alongside other legendary pirates.]]

Whitebeard was one of the most powerful pirates in history. In his prime, he was one of the few able to take on the Pirate King [[Gol D. Roger]], battling him for days to a draw.{{Qref|name=Whitebeard}}{{Qref|name=c966}} Due to his incredible strength, he was already feared as the '''"Strongest Man in the World"''', before Roger's death and the start of [[World Timeline#Great Age of Pirates|Great Age of Pirates]].{{Qref|name=vivre card}} After Roger's death, Whitebeard became one of the [[Four Emperors]], the four most powerful pirates in the world and the rulers of the [[New World]].{{Qref|name=Four Emperors mentioned}} In fact, among them, he was considered the '''"Closest Man to One Piece"''', and the ruler of the sea who stood before the "throne" and the title of Pirate King. Donquixote Doflamingo firmly believed that Whitebeard would have long since become the new Pirate King had he truly been interested in assuming that position.{{Qref|name=Whitebeard}}{{Qref|chap=801|ep=746|page=9}} As a testament to this, Whitebeard held not only the highest bounty among his peers, but the second highest in recorded history, at over 5 billion (only behind Roger's own).{{Qref|name=bounty}} [[Kaidou]], who is renowned as the world's '''"Strongest Creature"''', put Whitebeard in the same elite class as other legendary pirates, that actually possess the strength to stand against him in battle, such as Roger, [[Kouzuki Oden]], [[Shanks]], and their [[Rocks D. Xebec|former captain]].{{Qref|name=c1001}}

Even in his old age, he was able to effortlessly defeat [[Portgas D. Ace|Ace]] over a hundred times, even once while he was sleeping.{{Qref|chap=552|page=9-13|ep=461|Whitebeard defeats and recruits Ace.}} During the [[Summit War of Marineford]], Newgate's health was declining at a rapid rate due to his refusal to go into battle with life support and medication, despite this, he was able to engage in combat with [[Kuzan|Aokiji]],{{Qref|chap=553|page=6|ep=462|Aokiji attacks Whitebeard with Ice Block: Partisan.}} [[Borsalino|Kizaru]],{{Qref|chap=553|page=16|ep=463|Kizaru attacks Whitebeard with Yasakani no Magatama.}} and [[Sakazuki|Akainu]]{{Qref|name=Akainu Attacks}} on even terms. After Akainu killed Ace, Whitebeard brutally injured the Admiral in retaliation, with the latter being practically helpless in response to Whitebeard's power, temporarily defeating him in a relatively short battle with a mere two hits, causing immense destruction all around.{{Qref|chap=575|page=6-9|ep=484}} 

Whitebeard's reputation alone made his simple declaration of [[Fish-Man Island]] being his territory enough to keep [[Slavery|slave]] traders and pirates from attacking the island further, making Whitebeard himself far more effective than the treaty signed with the World Government 200 years before his death.{{Qref|name=Fish-Man Island}} People from every ocean were aware of the Emperor's power and seemingly believed that he could end the world if he so wished.{{Qref|chap=550|page=2-3|ep=459|Civilians from the Four Blues and the Grand Line speak of Whitebeard.}} Few would dare to challenge him or any of his crew, which makes Ace, [[Crocodile]], Aokiji, Akainu, [[Marshall D. Teach|Blackbeard]], Kaidou, and Luffy very brave and powerful people, for just trying. After his death, the entire world fell into chaos: with total victory declared for the Marines and all of Whitebeard's territories no longer considered dangerous (despite the fact that his crew was still alive).{{Qref|chap=581|ep=490}} 

As a true testament to his strength and reputation, the [[World Government]] was prepared to use practically the entire Marine force and the Seven Warlords of the Sea to fight Newgate and his crew, with Sengoku even remarking that their victory was not guaranteed due to Whitebeard's overwhelming power.{{Qref|chap=550|page=7-12|ep=459|The forces gathered at Marineford to combat Whitebeard are detailed.}}{{Qref|chap=552|page=18|ep=462|Sengoku claims Whitebeard has the power to destroy the world.}}

===Physical Abilities===
{{Cquote|Even in death, his body did not fall. His figure, taking down enemies while losing half of his head, was truly monstrous. The total number of sword wounds he received in this battle was 267. He was shot by 152 bullets and was hit by 46 cannonballs. And despite all this, his proud back, over the course of his entire life as a pirate, never received a single scar from running away!|Edward Newgate's death.{{Qref|name=Death Narration|chap=576|page=16-17|ep=485|A narration of Whitebeard's death.}}}}

[[File:Whitebeard Refusing Medical Treatment.png|thumb|left|210px|Whitebeard refuses to use his medical apparatus while his crew fusses over him.]]

Whitebeard was given the title of the '''"Strongest Man in the World"''' for his physical power, which is far superior to even a giant. During the [[Summit War of Marineford]], Whitebeard completely overpowered vast numbers of strong Marine officers and giants with tremendous physical might, such as Vice Admiral [[Lonz]], with only one hand and supplemented by his Devil Fruit powers.{{Qref|name=Lonz Defeat|chap=556|page=4-5|ep=465|Whitebeard defeats Lonz with one attack.}}{{Qref|name=Quake Naginata|chap=566|page=16-17|ep=475|Whitebeard defeats several dozen Marines with a quake-enhanced naginata swing.}}{{Qref|chap=569|page=10-11|ep=478|Whitebeard defeats dozens of Marines with a single attack.}} Whitebeard blocked a two-handed downward swing from the giant Vice Admiral [[John Giant]] with only one hand on his naginata,{{Qref|chap=564|page=6|ep=473|Whitebeard blocks John Giant's strike with one hand on his naginata.}} extinguished the flames of one of Akainu's molten rocks with just a single breath,{{Qref|chap=554|page=11|ep=463|Whitebeard extinguishes the flaming rock on the end of his naginata with a single breath.}} and prevented a massive paddle ship from advancing using only one hand.{{Qref|chap=572|page=12-13|ep=481|Whitebeard stops Squard's paddle ship from advancing.}} He could jump to great heights to attack large opponents, such as John Giant.{{Qref|chap=564|page=9|ep=473|Whitebeard knocks out John Giant with a shockwave.}} In his prime, Newgate was capable of fighting Roger to a standstill in a battle that lasted 3 days and 3 nights {{Qref|name=c966}} and instantly slice a [[Knight of God]] in half (although said Knight quickly regenerated from the attack). {{Qref|chap=1161|page=16|ep=}}

Despite his gigantic size, Whitebeard could move at considerable speeds, having appeared behind Akainu to attack him in a matter of seconds, with the latter (who was on his way to kill Luffy) only realizing it once his soldiers yelled at him to watch out.{{Qref|chap=575|page=6|ep=484|Whitebeard sneaks up on Akainu prior to attacking him.}}

Whitebeard appeared to have debilitating health problems, possibly stemming from his advanced age and excessive drinking. Furthermore, since Thatch is responsible for keeping his health in check with his cooking, Whitebeard's health deteriorates even faster after Thatch's death by the hands of Blackbeard.{{Qref|name=Novel|novel=a2|nchap=Prologue}} When not in battle, he was always surrounded by nurses, used oxygen tubes, and was hooked up to intravenous tubes and life support systems; despite this, he used to literally drink [[Foods/Beverages#Rice Brew ("Sake")|sake]] by the barrel.{{Qref|name=intro}} However, Marco noted that Whitebeard's health had gotten worse, and he no longer possessed the reflexes to avoid Squard's surprise attack, which was, in the past, something easy for him to achieve.{{Qref|name=Worsening|chap=563|page=11|ep=472|Marco notes that Whitebeard's health has deteriorated.}} Even with his health issues, Whitebeard was still considered the world's most dangerous and powerful pirate.

Whitebeard's physical resistance and pain tolerance were tremendous: he was able to keep fighting despite the number of life-threatening injuries he sustained, which included part of his head being burned off.{{Qref|name=Meigo Wound}} This also proves that Whitebeard possessed enormous amounts of stamina and endurance; no matter how much damage he took throughout the battle, Whitebeard continued to press forward and fight, only stopping once almost all of the [[Blackbeard Pirates]] collectively shot and brutally stabbed him to death at point-blank range.{{Qref|chap=576|page=10-11, 14-15|ep=485|Whitebeard is killed by the Blackbeard Pirates.}} It was shown that even in his old age, in a heavily wounded state and without access to his Devil Fruit and [[Haki]] powers, he could near-effortlessly take down a Warlord of the Sea, as demonstrated in his fight against Blackbeard.{{Qref|chap=576|page=8|ep=485|Whitebeard incapacitates Blackbeard with a single blow from his naginata.}}

During the Summit War, Whitebeard sustained 267 sword wounds, 152 gunshot wounds, and 46 wounds from cannonballs, and got a portion of his head blasted off, totaling 465 injuries in all.{{Qref|name=Death Narration}} In addition, he received one of Kizaru's laser beams{{Qref|chap=571|page=9|ep=480|Kizaru pierces Whitebeard with a laser beam.}} and two of Akainu's magma blasts.{{Qref|name=Akainu Attacks}}{{Qref|name=Meigo Wound}} Whitebeard also received a brutal assault from the Blackbeard Pirates. However, even after taking so much damage in his already weakened state, he died standing, an impressive feat when compared to other characters. Even Teach was shocked by Whitebeard's tenacity.{{Qref|chap=576|page=15|ep=485|Whitebeard dies.}}

===Tactical Skills===
Besides his formidable power, Whitebeard was a brilliant leader and an incredibly skilled military strategist: a match for former [[Marine Ranks#Fleet Admiral|Fleet Admiral]] [[Sengoku]], one renowned as "The Resourceful General" for his famed acumen on the field of battle. The Emperor's tactical prowess was demonstrated when he saw through Sengoku's deliberate leak of information regarding a change of schedule for Ace's execution,{{Qref|chap=558|page=3|ep=467|Whitebeard sees through Sengoku's scheme and refuses to fall for it.}} and when he foresaw the Pacifista's arrival at Marineford and scattered the pirates so that they would not be routed by the cyborgs.{{Qref|chap=562|page=3|ep=471|The pirates realize that Whitebeard scattered them so the Pacifista could not corner them.}}

In addition, Whitebeard could easily adapt to rapidly changing situations even in the heat of battle, as shown when he bypassed a siege wall impervious to his Devil Fruit powers by having Oars, who was in a near-death state, help carry the paddle ship into the Marineford plaza.{{Qref|chap=566|page=10-14|ep=475|Whitebeard uses Oars and a hidden paddle ship to bypass the siege wall.}} Even when he was on the brink of death, Whitebeard quickly thought of a countermeasure against Teach's Devil Fruit power's nullification abilities by using his naginata to cut Teach down, taking him off-guard for him to use his quake powers to injure him.

===Devil Fruit===
{{See|Gura Gura no Mi}}

[[File:Whitebeard Using Gura Gura no Mi Ability.png|thumb|210px|Whitebeard uses the Gura Gura no Mi.]]

Whitebeard ate the Gura Gura no Mi, a [[Paramecia]]-type [[Devil Fruit]] that allowed him to generate powerful shockwaves and earthquakes.{{Qref|chap=552|page=17|ep=462|Whitebeard is identified as having eaten the Gura Gura no Mi.}} This power is considered to be the strongest Devil Fruit power within the Paramecia class.{{Qref|sbs=58|Oda classifies the Gura Gura no Mi as the strongest Paramecia-type fruit.|page=24}} According to [[Sengoku]], Whitebeard had the power to destroy the world.{{Qref|chap=552|page=18|ep=462|Sengoku claims Whitebeard has the power to destroy the world.}}

He had the power to send incredibly powerful shockwaves through the air, creating cracks in the air itself in the process. These shockwaves possess devastating offensive might, being able to clash evenly with the [[Magu Magu no Mi]], the Devil Fruit with the highest attack power out of all the Devil Fruits.{{Qref|chap=567|page=15|ep=476|Whitebeard counters Akainu's Dai Funka with a shockwave.}} He could use these shockwaves to quickly take down multiple enemies over a widespread area or take down a single target with terrifying effectiveness, even [[Giants]]. He could also use his shockwaves defensively, as their vast raw power could easily stop incoming attacks. He could also generate strong vibrations from his body that could easily shatter ice.{{Qref|chap=553|page=6-7|ep=462|Whitebeard counters Aokiji's Ice Block: Partisan and shatters Aokiji himself with a shockwave.}}{{Qref|chap=567|page=4|ep=476|Whitebeard's vibrations prevent him from being frozen by Aokiji's Ice Ball.}}

[[File:Gura Gura Island Quake.png|thumb|left|210px|An entire island and the surrounding sea being tilted.]]

He could use his power to shake, rupture, and tilt the landscape itself. By striking at the general area with his quake powers, he could cause large earthquakes and, under the right circumstances, massive tsunamis.{{Qref|chap=552|page=17-19|ep=462|Whitebeard's shockwaves create tsunamis on either side of Marineford.}} His quakes would cause serious damage and alterations to the surrounding landscape, destroying buildings, creating large crevices in the ground, and pushing up fragments of the ground into new rock formations. He could even "grab" the surrounding area itself and tilt it, described as making the entire sea tilt.{{Qref|chap=564|page=6-9|ep=473|Whitebeard uses Shima Yurashi to tilt Marineford and the surrounding ocean.}}

Whitebeard could use his power to enhance his physical attacks by surrounding his hands and feet with concentrated quake bubbles.{{Qref|name=Lonz Defeat}} These quake bubbles would release a small but powerful shockwave on impact, greatly increasing the destructive power of his melee attacks. He could also surround the blade of his polearm with a quake bubble, greatly increasing its destructive power as well.{{Qref|name=Quake Naginata}}

Soon after Whitebeard's death, his power was stolen by Blackbeard through unknown means.{{Qref|chap=577|page=13-15|ep=486|Blackbeard reveals he has stolen the power of the Gura Gura no Mi.}}

===Haki===
{{Main|Haki}}

Whitebeard was one of the very few people in the world who could use all three types of Haki.

====Supreme King Haki====
[[File:Newgate's Haki.png|thumb|200x200px|Whitebeard infusing Murakumogiri with Supreme King Haki.]]

Whitebeard possessed immense mastery in the usage of [[Haki/Supreme King Haki|Supreme King Haki]].{{Qref|chap=570|page=2|ep=479|Fossa notes that Luffy possesses Supreme King Haki like Whitebeard and Shanks do.}} During his initial encounter with [[Kouzuki Oden]] 30 years ago, their sudden clash created a notable effect similar to lightning and released a large burst.{{Qref|name=c963|chap=963|page=16-17|ep=963|Oden and Whitebeard clash.}} His Supreme King Haki was displayed to a far greater extent against his longtime rival, [[Gol D. Roger]], as their clashing Supreme King Haki cracked the air, creating an effect akin to lightning and generating a shock wave that blew back everything and everyone on and near the island. Most notably, Newgate was one of the small "handful" of people capable of using the advanced application of "infusing" his attacks with Supreme King Haki, which exponentially increased his attack power, with his naginata being shown emitting streams of black lightning-like energy which caused their clash to disperse the clouds nearby.{{Qref|name=c966|chap=966|page=4-6|ep=965|ep2=966}}{{Qref|chap=1010|page=12-17|ep=1028|The advanced application of Supreme King Haki coating is explained and demonstrated.}} Another example was his clash with Shanks which resulted in the heavens being split in two.{{Qref|chap=434|ep=316|page=15-17|Whitebeard and Shanks' clash causes the heavens to split.}} 

During the Summit War, he was on the verge of using Supreme King Haki against some of the World Government's executioners to protect [[Portgas D. Ace]] but failed because of a sudden illness attack.{{Qref|chap=569|page=13|ep=478|Whitebeard attempts to use Supreme King Haki, but fails.}} He is capable of using this form of Haki in the video games ''[[One Piece: Pirate Warriors 2]],'' ''[[One Piece: Pirate Warriors 3|3]] and [[One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4|4]]'' as well as ''[[One Piece: Burning Blood]]''.

====Armament Haki====
[[File:Roger vs. Newgate.png|thumb|left|210px|Whitebeard and Roger clash with Haki-imbued weapons.]]

Whitebeard was an immensely skilled user of [[Haki/Armament Haki|Armament Haki]], which he could imbue his weapon Murakumogiri with. Two decades ago in his prime, he was shown clashing evenly with the samurai [[Kouzuki Oden]] who was a powerful Armament Haki user in his own right.{{Qref|name=c963}} Whitebeard could also utilize the advanced technique of projecting Haki out from his blade; this was shown during his fight with Roger where the duo's weapons met in a powerful clash without even making contact.{{Qref|name=c966}} 

In the anime, when Whitebeard used advanced Armament Haki, it is shown as a red-colored flowing aura.

Due to his age and worsening health, it was not as powerful compared to his prime, but he could still negate the intangibility of Logia-based Devil Fruits. In the past, he was able to defeat Crocodile (though it is unknown if the former [[Seven Warlords of the Sea|Warlord of the Sea]] had eaten his [[Suna Suna no Mi|Devil Fruit]] by that point).{{Qref|chap=563|page=11|ep=472|Crocodile reveals that Whitebeard defeated him in the past.}} During the Summit War, Whitebeard successfully inflicted significant damage on [[Sakazuki|Akainu]],{{Qref|chap=575|page=6-7|ep=484|Whitebeard brutally injures Akainu for killing Ace.}} whereas [[Polo Marco|Marco]], [[Vista]], and Jinbe—highly skilled Armament Haki users themselves—failed to do so.{{Qref|chap=574|page=7|ep=483|Marco and Vista attack Akainu with Armament Haki, but fail to harm him.}}

====Observation Haki====
Whitebeard was an extremely skilled user of [[Haki/Observation Haki|Observation Haki]]. It was first shown 30 years prior after both he and the [[Whitebeard Pirates]] shipwrecked in Wano, as he could sense [[Kouzuki Oden|Oden]] coming from a vast distance towards them, and his overall strength.{{Qref|name=c963p15}}{{Qref|name=vivre card}} He was even able to sense and counter Ace (when he was still new on the ship and was attempting to kill Newgate) while sleeping. In the bay of Marineford, he predicted Crocodile's sudden attack but did not move, knowing that Luffy would block it.{{Qref|chap=557|page=13-14|ep=466|Whitebeard predicts but does not respond to Crocodile's surprise attack because Luffy defends him.}} However, due to both his age and worsening health, he failed to predict Squard's betrayal and thus got injured,{{Qref|chap=562|ep=471|Whitebeard fails to avoid Squard's sword.}} something which, according to Marco, was totally unexpected from the Emperor.{{Qref|name=Worsening}}{{-}}

===Weapons===
{{See|Murakumogiri}}

[[File:Whitebeard Swings His Bisento.png|thumb|210px|Whitebeard swings Murakumogiri in conjunction with his Devil Fruit powers.]]

Whitebeard wielded a gigantic naginata called Murakumogiri, one of the [[Famous Blade#12 Supreme Grade Blades|12 Supreme Grade Blades]]. He was immensely skilled with this blade even in old age. He could use Murakumogiri to fight off countless powerful Marines in Marineford, including Marine Admirals, and during his prime, he also clashed with [[Kouzuki Oden]], one of the strongest [[samurai]] of Wano.

During his childhood in [[Sphinx (Location)|Sphinx]], his standard weapon was an improvised spear, made from a simple knife bound to a pole.

==Anime and Manga Differences==
===Appearance===
In the manga and other related merchandise, the interior color of Whitebeard's coat was initially green. In the anime and other related merchandise, it is red. Later in the manga, however, this was changed to red.{{Qref|vol=57|The color of the insides of Whitebeard's coat is changed to red on the cover.}} In his initial appearance in the anime, his eyes were black like many male characters of the series, but this was changed to a golden yellow color by the [[Summit War of Marineford]].

In the manga, Whitebeard has no hair showing, but in the anime, he initially had some brown hair; his hair was later retconned to follow the manga. His pants were also left hanging over his boots in his first appearance in the anime and during one of the scenes of his meeting with Shanks; in the manga, his pants were always tucked inside his boots.

===War at Marineford===
After Ace's death, Whitebeard tried to stop [[Sakazuki|Akainu]] but was attacked by [[Borsalino|Kizaru]]. In [[Episode 484]], instead of burning off a portion of Whitebeard's head, Akainu only managed to remove part of Whitebeard's mustache. Instead, Akainu successfully punched another hole in Whitebeard's torso and visibly filled him with magma. Also, the battle between Whitebeard and Akainu went on longer, with Whitebeard launching more vicious attacks against the [[Admiral]].{{Qref|ep=484|Whitebeard's fight against Akainu and the wounds he receives from the latter are altered in the anime.}} The fight between Whitebeard and [[Marshall D. Teach|Blackbeard]] is extended in the anime. Blackbeard manages to land punches on Whitebeard's torso and chin. Even after the initial strike proved Whitebeard's quake punch has no effect on Blackbeard, Whitebeard continued to punch several more times before using his naginata. Whitebeard was unable to move after his last attack on Blackbeard but managed to move forward with his body turned red with smoke coming out of it, similar to [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]] in [[Gomu Gomu no Mi/Gear 2 Techniques|Gear 2]]. This was likely done to signify his fury. Additionally, Whitebeard's speech about [[One Piece]] was longer in the anime.{{Qref|ep=485|Whitebeard's battle against Blackbeard and speech about One Piece are altered in the anime.}}

[[File:Whitebeard's Death in the Anime.png|thumb|210px|Whitebeard's death in the anime.]]

After Whitebeard's death, when the narrator lists all the injuries Whitebeard suffered, swords that have pierced his front and through his body could be seen with the tips protruding from his back. In the anime, there were no swords at all in his body.

[[File:Whitebeard Anime Death Newspaper.png|thumb|left|210px|Whitebeard's body in the newspaper.]]

Later, in [[Episode 507]], when [[Usopp]] dropped a [[newspaper]] covering the aftermath of the war, Whitebeard's body was shown to match the manga's depiction as opposed to the anime's censorships: his torso had swords sticking out, he was posed to make it looks like a portion of his head was torn off, and the gaping hole on his stomach that Akainu inflicted on him in the anime was missing, leaving only the hole in his upper chest.{{-}}

==Translation and Dub Issues==
Some minor debate exists as to whether ''Whitebeard'' is the "proper" translation of the epithet {{Nihongo|''Shirohige''|白ひげ}}, as Newgate does not wear an actual beard. This discrepancy stems from the Japanese term {{Nihongo|''Hige''|{{ruby|髭|ひげ}}}} being a generic term for facial hair that applies to both mustaches and beards; however, since few (if any) serious alternatives have been offered, both fans and professional translations continue to use ''Whitebeard'', as does the quasi-canon ''[[One Piece Yellow: Grand Elements|One Piece Yellow]]'' databook.

While [[4Kids Entertainment]] never dubbed any of his appearances in the anime proper, some tie-in materials indicate that it planned to rename him ''Ward'' Newgate.{{Qref|name=4Kids}}

==Inspirations and Influences==
Newgate's surname ''Edward'' was taken from the infamous {{W|Blackbeard|"Blackbeard" Edward Teach}}, [[Eiichiro Oda]]'s personal favorite pirate from real life.{{Qref|name=surname|sbs=49|page=88|The origin of Newgate's surname is revealed.}}

Per the second installment of [[One Para]] (later reprinted in [[One Piece Green: Secret Pieces|databook ''Green'']]), Newgate's character was directly modeled after the barkeeper of a pub Oda used to frequent with a previous manager. This barkeeper, who often wore breathing tubes while telling war stories, passed away in 2007.{{Qref|other=OP|Vol. 2 (originally bundled with first-run copies of [[One Piece Yellow: Grand Elements|databook ''Yellow'']]) reveals Whitebeard's inspiration.}}{{Qref|data=green|page=346}}

==Trivia==
[[File:Whitebeard and Ace's Graves at Universal Studios Japan.png|thumb|200px|Newgate and Ace's graves made by Universal Studios of Japan.]]
*{{W|Universal Studios|Universal Studios}} of Japan built a replica of [[Portgas D. Ace|Ace]]'s and Newgate's tombs. Newgate's epitaph reads: ''"Edward Newgate, captain of the Whitebeard pirates, here lies a great captain and father, liberated from the exhausting role and labor, who captained the Moby Dick in the spectacular Era of Pirates"''.
*Newgate is widely regarded as the "strongest man" in the world. In comparison, [[Kaidou]] is said to be the "strongest creature" in the world.
*True to Whitebeard's refusal to truly fall down even once during battle, in video games when he is knocked down, he instead falls on one knee at most.
*Newgate's given name was possibly inspired by {{W|London}}'s notorious {{W|Newgate Prison}}, which incarcerated and executed many famous outlaws, including iconic pirates such as {{W|William Kidd}} and several crewmen of "King of the Pirates" {{W|Henry Every}}. Indeed, its charges were publicized by a series of {{W|chapbooks}}, ''{{W|The Newgate Calendar}}'', that remained wildly popular into the {{W|Victorian era}}.
*In the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, and 7th [[Popularity Polls|fan polls]] of most popular characters, Newgate was ranked 43rd, 69th, 26th, 28th, and 31st, respectively.
*At 72 years old, Newgate was the oldest known member of the Four Emperors.
*Newgate held the highest [[bounty]] among the Four Emperors (both past and present), and the second-highest recorded bounty among all pirates, surpassed only by Roger.
**In his bounty of {{B}}5,0'''46''',000,000, the 4-6 can be read as ''shi-ro'', referencing the term for {{Nihongo|white|白|Shiro}}.
*Newgate shares several characteristics with the legendary warrior monk {{W|Benkei|Musashibo Benkei}}. A popular figure in Japanese folklore, Benkei was said to have been five times the size of a normal man, possessed inhuman strength, and wielded a naginata as his weapon of choice. He famously died in battle standing upright, with his body riddled with arrows and spears.
*Interestingly, a crescent-shaped mustache was also the key trait of Luffy's earliest enemy: [[Gally|Crescent-Moon Gally]], main antagonist of Eiichiro Oda's [[Romance Dawn, Version 1|first ''Romance Dawn'' prototype]].
*Newgate's favorite foods are {{W|Alcoholic beverage|alcoholic beverages}} and {{W|Food prices|cheap food}}{{Qref|name=vivre card}}, and his least favorite food is {{W|Kopi luwak|kopi luwak}}.{{Qref|name=vc2|data=vivre card|card=0270|Newgate's Vivre Card entry (ver. Exciting! Legendary Men!!).}}
*Newgate's animal resemblance is a {{W|Beluga whale|white whale}} (alluding to the name of [[Moby Dick|his flagship]]).{{Qref|name=vc2}}
*Newgate's hobby is saving.{{Qref|name=vc2}}

===SBS-Based Trivia===
*Newgate's birthday, April 6, comes from his epithet's Japanese transcription first and second syllables since 4-6 can be derived from shi-ro, meaning "white".{{Qref|name=sbs57}}
*Newgate's namesake, {{W|Blackbeard|Edward Teach}}, also inspired the names of both [[Marshall D. Teach]] (the in-universe "Blackbeard") and [[Thatch]] (''Edward Thatch'' being an alternative name, possibly alias, for the historical Teach).{{Qref|name=surname}}
*Oda stated that Newgate wishes all the [[Doctor|Nurses]] of the world wore Leopard Print stockings.{{Qref|sbs=28|page=124|The reason Whitebeard's Nurses wear Leopard Print stockings.}}
*Oda jokingly stated that Newgate once had a dog, [[Stefan]], with a near-identical mustache.{{Qref|sbs=58|page=24|Fan question: When does Whitebeard use the boomerang he's got under his nose?}}
